## 📌 **Early Life & Education (1943–1972)**  
**October 29, 1943** – Born in Seattle, Washington  
- Parents: June Hazel (housewife), Russell J. Simpson (Boeing mechanic)  
- Raised in Juneau, Alaska  
- Strict Baptist upbringing; attended church 4–5 times/week  
- Called himself a "straight-A Bible student"  

**1960s** – Attended West Anchorage High School  
**1968** – Majored in English at the University of Oregon  

**Post-University (1970s)**  
- Worked as a ski instructor in Utah  
- Moved to San Francisco  
- Worked at a theatrical advertising agency  
- Did public relations for the First International Erotic Film Festival  

> 🔗 *Transition Note:* Early exposure to film and adult entertainment laid groundwork for future industry connections and controversial behavior.

---

## 📌 **Entry into Hollywood (1972–1977)**  
**1972** – Joined **Jack Wodell & Associates** in San Francisco  
- Transitioned to **Warner Bros.** as marketing executive  
- Handled distribution marketing for *Woodstock* (1970) and *A Clockwork Orange* (1971)  

**1975** – Interviewed at **Paramount Pictures**  
- Referred by friend Steve Tisch (nephew of Larry Tisch)  
- Jerry Bruckheimer loaned him his car for the interview  

**1976** – Co-wrote and had a small role in *Cannonball* (Paramount)  
- First major writing credit and on-screen appearance  

**1977** – Named **Vice-President of Production** at Paramount  
**1981** – Promoted to **President of Production**  

> 🔗 *Causality Link:* Early success at Paramount built his reputation, but also exposed his volatile behavior.

---

## 📌 **Professional Downfall at Paramount (1982)**  
**1982** – Fired from Paramount  
- Passed out during a studio meeting due to **drug use**  
- Working on **eight films simultaneously**  
- Known for **tantrums during production**  

> 🔗 *Turning Point:* Drug use and erratic behavior led to professional dismissal — a direct catalyst for seeking new partnerships.

---

## 📌 **Partnership with Jerry Bruckheimer (1982–1995)**  
**1982–1983** – Forged partnership with **Jerry Bruckheimer**  
- Shared vision for high-grossing, action-driven blockbusters  
- Co-produced major hits:  
  - *Flashdance* (1983)  
  - *Beverly Hills Cop* (1984)  
  - *Top Gun* (1986)  
  - *Beverly Hills Cop II* (1987)  

**1985 & 1988** – Named **Producers of the Year** by National Association of Theatre Owners (NATO)  

**1985** – Launched their own production company (affiliated with Paramount)  

> 🔗 *Causality Link:* Partnership emerged after Paramount failure — a pivot to success through shared ambition and risk-taking.

## 📌 **Paramount Deal & Dispute (1990)**  
**1990** – Signed **5-year deal with Paramount** worth **$300 million**  
- Produced *Days of Thunder* (1990), starring Tom Cruise  
- Film received **mixed reviews**, grossed **$158M** (on $60M budget)  
- **Underperformed** compared to prior hits  
- **Disagreement over blame**:  
  - Simpson/Bruckheimer blamed Paramount for rushed planning  
  - Paramount blamed overspending and poor management  

**Result**: Partnership with Paramount ended shortly after  

> 🔗 *Causality Link:* Financial underperformance exposed cracks in their production model and strained studio relations.
